newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TVNZ reports record NZ$22.86 mln H1 net profit.
newsitem.headline: TVNZ reports record NZ$22.86 mln H1 net profit.

text.p: Television New Zealand on Tuesday reported a record NZ$22.86 million after tax profit for the six months to June, compared to NZ$15.59 million in the corresponding period last year.
This was an increase of 46.7 percent.
Turnover was NZ$206.23 million, a rise of $15.22 million over the previous year.
TVNZ chairman Norman Geary said the record performance came on the back of increased turnover coupled with more effectiveness and efficiency in most areas, despite a soft demand for advertising.

"Taking into account the cost of developing (regional television network) Horizon Pacific Television, the dramatically increased cost of our rugby broadcast rights and the challenging advertising market, this is a highly satisfactory result," Geary said.

Geary said the board and management considered the strategy adopted last year to focus on the television business and the restructuring of the company into three operating divisions was the appropriate one.
"The company has excellent core competencies which will provide a sound base for profitable growth in New Zealand and overseas."
Overall, the company's operating divisions were performing well.
"We are focusing on free-to-air television based on our core competencies.

"We are also looking to Australia and beyond for growth opportunities in programme sales and transmission expertise, such as the $60 million contract Broadcast Communications Ltd, a TVNZ subsidiary, won to supply maintenance to the Australian National Transmission Agency," Geary said.-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
